zh: 惟有那名代表漕帮说话的尖丁，大摇其头。不过他首先声明，他自己有点意见，并有代表漕帮，不知该说不该说？
en: Only the headman who had spoken for the associations shook his head firmly. Before explaining, however, he made it clear that he had a personal opinion and was not speaking on behalf of the associations. He was unsure whether he ought to express it.

zh: “说，说！集思广益，说出来商量。”
en: “Go on! We need everyone's ideas. Tell us, and we can discuss it.”

zh: 照那尖丁个人的看法，漕船要能开行，首先得要疏浚河床，同时在各支流加闸，提高运河中的水位，然后另雇民船分载漕米，减轻漕船的载重，这样双管齐下，才有“动”的可能。
en: In the headman's personal view, getting the boats moving would first require dredging the channel and installing gates on the tributaries to raise the water level in the canal. Civilian boats would then have to be hired to take part of the grain and lighten the official vessels. Only by combining these two measures would movement be possible.

zh: “那就这样办啊！有何不可呢？”有个押运官兴奋地说。
en: “Then let us do precisely that! What is there to prevent us?” one escort official exclaimed excitedly.

zh: 那尖丁苦笑了一下，没有作声。椿寿却明白他的意思，以讥嘲的口吻答道：“老兄说得容易！可知道这一来要多少钱？”
en: The headman gave a bitter smile and said nothing. Chunshou, however, understood. “You make it sound easy,” he replied sarcastically. “Have you any idea what it would cost?”

zh: “于其赔累，何不把赔累的钱，花在疏浚河床和雇用民船上？不但交的差，而且治理了运河，也是大人的劳绩。”
en: “Rather than pay compensation, why not spend the money on dredging and hiring boats? That would not only fulfil the transport obligation but improve the canal as well. It would be an achievement to Your Excellency's credit.”

zh: 这两句话说动了椿寿的心，点着头沉吟，“这倒也是一说。”他自语似的问：“就不知道要多少日子？”
en: The argument appealed to Chunshou. He nodded thoughtfully. “There is something in that,” he murmured. “The question is how long it would take.”

zh: 疏浚的计划，施工的日程，要多少工、多少料，都要仔细计算，才能知道确数，在这样人多口杂的场台中，是不可能得到结果的，所以椿寿叫大家散一散，别外找了些实际能负责，能办事的人来重作商量。
en: The dredging plan, the construction schedule, and the labour and materials required all had to be carefully calculated before a definite answer could be given. Nothing of the sort could be settled in a crowded meeting where everyone was talking. Chunshou therefore dismissed the gathering and summoned a smaller group of people who could actually take responsibility and get things done.

zh: 这个少数人的集议，首先要谈的就是工料的来源。这实在也只有一个字：钱。漕帮中被推派出来说话的那名尖丁，以久历江湖的经验，预感到此举不妥，但人微言轻，无法扭转椿寿的“如意算盘”，便很干脆地答应了所派的经费，而且保证漕帮一定全力支持这件事。不过他也很郑重地声明，漕帮出了这笔钱，漕船不管如何非走不可。如果再出了什么花样。漕帮不能负责。
en: Their first concern was where the labour and materials would come from. In the end, that came down to a single word: money. Drawing on his long experience of the world, the headman who had represented the associations sensed that the undertaking would end badly. But a man of his low standing had little influence and could not overturn Chunshou's hopeful calculations. He therefore readily accepted the sum assigned to the associations and promised their full support. At the same time, he made one solemn condition: once they paid this money, the boats had to sail, come what might. If anything else went wrong, the associations would accept no further liability.

zh: 于是疏浚河道的计划，很快地便见诸实际行动。这件事地方官原来也有责任，只是湖州府和运河所经的乌程、归安、德清三县，要办这件事惟有派工派料。公文往返，以及召集绅士磋商，需要好久才能动工，未免缓不济急。
en: The dredging scheme was soon put into effect. The local authorities had responsibilities in the matter too, but Huzhou prefecture and the three counties through which the canal passed—Wucheng, Gui'an, and Deqing—could act only by requisitioning labour and materials. The exchange of official documents and consultations with local gentry would take so long that work could not begin soon enough to meet the emergency.

zh: 为了与天争时，自己拿钱出来征雇民工是最切实的办法。等这一切安排好了，预计八月底以前，漕船一定可以开行。这样，椿寿才算松了一口气，动身回省。
en: With time running out, the most practical solution was to supply the money themselves and hire local labourers. Once these arrangements were made, it was estimated that the boats would certainly be able to sail before the end of the eighth month. Only then did Chunshou breathe more easily and set off for the provincial capital.

zh: 走的那天，秋风秋雨，一般行旅闷损不乐的天气，在椿寿却大为高兴，心里在想，这雨最好落大些，连下几天，前溪水涨，起漕的时间，还好提前。
en: On the day he left, autumn wind and rain made the weather miserable for most travellers. Chunshou, however, was delighted. Let the rain grow heavier, he thought, and continue for several days. If the streams ahead rose, the grain boats might depart even sooner.

zh: * * *回到省城，他第一件事便是去见抚台黄宗汉。
en: On returning to the provincial capital, his first act was to call on Governor Huang Zonghan.

zh: 听完报告，黄宗汉还夸奖了一番，说他实心办事。还告诉他一些京里来的消息，说朝廷已有旨意，严饬直隶总督和驻北通州的仓场侍郎，自天津杨村地方，调派一千五百艘驳船到山东临清，准备驳运漕粮。不过直隶总督已经复奏，怕杨村的驳船，到达临清，河水已经结冰，所以这样请求：江浙的漕粮在临清、德州一带卸下来，暂时存贮，到明年开春解冻，再转漕北上，这个请求，能不能奉准，尚不可知。
en: After hearing his report, Huang actually praised his conscientious work. He also passed on news from the capital. The court had ordered the governor-general of Zhili and the granary vice-minister stationed at North Tongzhou to send fifteen hundred barges from Yangcun near Tianjin to Linqing in Shandong, ready to take over the grain. The governor-general of Zhili had replied, however, that the river might be frozen by the time the Yangcun barges reached Linqing. He proposed that the grain from Jiangsu and Zhejiang be unloaded around Linqing and Dezhou and stored there until the spring thaw, then sent north. Whether the request would be approved was not yet known.

zh: 椿寿认为这是个好消息，他原有顾虑，怕北地天寒，到了十月以后，河里结冰，漕船依旧受阻。现在既有直隶总督据实奏陈，等于为他把心里想说的话说了出来，格于事实，朝廷不能不准，这样就只要到了临清，便算达成任务。倘说迟延，则各地情形相同，处分的案子混在一起，变成“通案”就不要紧了。
en: Chunshou regarded this as good news. He had been worried that the northern cold would freeze the rivers after the tenth month and leave the grain boats obstructed once again. Now the governor-general of Zhili had reported the facts, effectively saying what Chunshou himself had wanted to say. Faced with reality, the court could scarcely refuse. Reaching Linqing would therefore count as completion of the task. As for any delay, conditions were the same for everyone. The disciplinary cases would be combined into a general case, and the matter would lose its danger.

zh: 椿寿吃了这颗定心丸，对于疏浚河道的工程，进度不甚理想，就不太着急。他最关心的是直隶总督那个复奏的下文，等漕船开出，才看到明发上谕：“浙江嘉杭等帮米石，如能拨船赶运，当仍遵前旨，酌拨杨村船只，趁此天气晴和，迅往拨运。设或沿途必须截卸，临情、德州等仓，是否足资容纳？着仓场侍郎、直隶总督、漕运总督、山东巡抚各将现在应办急务，迅速妥为办理，毋得听任属员推诿恶习，各分畛域，再赴贻误。懔之！“
en: With this reassurance, Chunshou became less anxious about the unsatisfactory progress of the dredging. What interested him most was the response to the governor-general's memorial. Only after the boats had sailed did he see the publicly circulated imperial edict: “If the rice carried by the Jiaxing, Hangzhou, and other Zhejiang fleets can be expedited by allocating additional vessels, the previous order shall remain in force. A suitable number of boats from Yangcun shall be sent promptly to transfer it while the weather remains fine and mild. Should unloading en route prove unavoidable, do the granaries at Linqing, Dezhou, and elsewhere have sufficient capacity? The granary vice-minister, the governor-general of Zhili, the director-general of grain transport, and the governor of Shandong shall each promptly and properly attend to the urgent duties before them. They must not permit their subordinates to persist in shirking responsibility, confining themselves to their own jurisdictions, and causing further delay. Let them take heed!”

zh: “亏得赶运出去。”椿寿心里在想，“照上谕来看，在临清、德州截卸，暂时存贮，已经准了。不过粮仓恐怕不够，湖帮的漕米到了那里，倘或无仓可储，倒是棘手之事。”
en: “Thank goodness we got the boats away,” Chunshou thought. “The edict appears to allow them to unload at Linqing and Dezhou for temporary storage. But there may not be enough granary space. If the Huzhou grain arrives and there is nowhere to put it, we shall have a difficult problem.”

zh: 于是，他“上院”去见抚台。黄宗汉一见他就说：“啊，来得正好。我正要叫‘戈什哈’去请你，有件要紧事商量。”
en: He therefore went to see the governor. As soon as Huang saw him, he said, “Ah, just in time! I was about to send an attendant for you. There is an important matter we must discuss.”

zh: “请大人吩咐。”
en: “Please give me your instructions, Your Excellency.”

zh: “不，不！你有事你先说。”
en: “No, no. If you have business, speak first.”

zh: 椿寿便说明来意，意思是想请抚台出奏，浙江湖属八帮的漕米，已出省境北上。如果到了临清，无法驳运，需要截卸时，请饬下漕运总督及山东巡抚，预留空仓。他是怕湖属八帮的漕船最后到达，仓位为他帮捷足先登，所以有此要求。
en: Chunshou explained why he had come. He wished the governor to submit a memorial stating that the grain boats of Huzhou's eight associations had left Zhejiang and were heading north. If they reached Linqing but could not transfer their cargo and had to unload it, the director-general of grain transport and the governor of Shandong should be instructed to reserve empty granaries. Chunshou feared that the Huzhou boats would arrive last, after other fleets had occupied all the available space.

zh: 黄宗汉一面听，一面不断摇头，等他说完，俯身向前问道：“漕运一事，贵司内行，而且今年由贵司一手料理，我要请问，可曾计算过‘回空’的日子？”
en: Huang shook his head repeatedly as he listened. When Chunshou finished, he leaned forward. “You are the expert on grain transport, and this year you have managed it entirely yourself. May I ask whether you have calculated when the empty boats will return?”

zh: 原来是这一层顾虑，椿寿略略放了心，“回大人的话，”他说，“回空自然要衍期……”
en: So that was his concern. Chunshou felt a little relieved. “Your Excellency, their return will naturally be delayed...”

zh: “衍期多少时候？”黄宗汉不待辞毕，枪着问道，“请贵司算与我听一听。”
en: “By how long?” Huang interrupted. “Please work it out for me.”

zh: “这要看临清的情形。如果在那里截卸，等明年开冻驳运，又要看前面漕船的多寡，多则慢，少则快。
en: “That depends on conditions at Linqing. If the grain is unloaded there and transferred after the thaw next year, it will also depend on the number of boats ahead of ours. The more there are, the longer it will take.”

zh: “最快什么时候？”
en: “What is the earliest possible date?”

zh: “总要到明年四月。”
en: “Not before the fourth month of next year.”

zh: “回空呢？”
en: “And the return journey?”

zh: “也要两个月。”
en: “That would take another two months.”

zh: “这就是说，漕船明年夏天才能回家，还要经过一番修补，又得费个把月，最快也得在七月里才能到各县受兑漕米。请问贵司，明年新漕，不是又跟今年一样，迟到八九月才能启运吗？”
en: “So the boats will not return home until next summer. They will then need repairs, which will take another month or so. At the earliest, they will not be ready to collect grain from the counties until the seventh month. Tell me, then: will next year's new grain not be delayed until the eighth or ninth month, just like this year's?”

zh: “是！”椿寿答道，“不过明年改用海运，亦无关系。”
en: “Yes,” Chunshou answered. “But next year we shall use sea transport, so it will not matter.”

zh: “什么叫没有关系？”黄宗汉勃然变色，“你说得好轻巧。年年把漕期延后，何时始得恢复正常？须知今年是贵司责无旁贷，明年就完全是我的责任。贵司这样子做法，简直是有意跟我过不去呀！”
en: “What do you mean, it will not matter?” Huang's expression changed sharply. “You speak very lightly of it. If the schedule slips later every year, when will it ever return to normal? This year's responsibility rests squarely on you; next year's will be entirely mine. The way you are handling this, one would think you were deliberately trying to make trouble for me!”

zh: 椿寿一看抚台变脸，大出意外，他亦是旗下公子哥儿出身，一个忍不住，当即顶撞了过去：“大人言重了！既然我责无旁贷，该杀该剐，自然由我负责，大人何必如此气急败坏？”
en: The governor's sudden anger took Chunshou completely by surprise. He too had been raised as a privileged bannerman, and for a moment he lost his restraint. “Your Excellency goes too far! If the responsibility is mine, then I shall answer for it, even if I must be executed. There is no need for Your Excellency to lose his temper in this fashion.”

zh: “好，好！”黄宗汉一半真的生气，一半有意做作，脸上一阵青，一阵红地说：“你负责，你负责！请教，这责任如何负法？”
en: “Very well! Very well!” Huang was partly angry and partly acting. His face alternated between pallor and a flush. “You will answer for it, will you? May I ask how?”

zh: “本年漕运虽由我主管，但自从大人到任，凡事亦曾禀命而行。今年江苏试办海运，成效甚佳，请大人出奏，明年浙省仿照江苏成例，不就行了吗？“
en: “Although I have supervised this year's grain transport, since Your Excellency arrived I have acted only after reporting to you. Jiangsu's trial of sea transport has been highly successful this year. If Your Excellency requests permission for Zhejiang to follow its example next year, would that not settle the matter?”

zh: “哼，哼！”黄宗汉不断冷笑，“看贵司的话，好象军机大臣的口吻，我倒再要请教，如果上头不准呢？”
en: “Hmph! Hmph!” Huang kept giving cold little laughs. “You speak as though you were a grand councillor. Then let me ask another question: what if the throne refuses?”

zh: “没有不准之理。”
en: “There is no reason it should refuse.”

zh: “又是这样的口吻！”黄宗汉一拍炕几，大声呵斥，“你到底是来议事，还是来抬杠？”
en: “That tone again!” Huang struck the small table on the couch and shouted, “Have you come to discuss business or to argue with me?”

zh: 椿寿做了二十几年的官，从未见过这样的上司，心里在想：你是科甲出身，我亦不是捐班佐杂爬上来的，受惯了气的，论宦途经历，我放浙江藩司，你还不过是浙江臬司，只不过朝中有人，道光十五年乙未那一榜……
en: In more than twenty years of official service, Chunshou had never encountered such a superior. You entered through the examinations, he thought, but I am not some subordinate who bought his way in and has grown accustomed to being insulted. As for our careers, when I was appointed provincial treasurer of Zhejiang, you were still only its judicial commissioner. You merely have people at court—the men from that yiwei examination of the fifteenth year of Daoguang...

zh: 转念到此，椿寿打了个寒噤，暗叫一声：大事不好！黄宗汉的同年，已有当了军机大臣的，那是苏州的彭蕴章。还有户部两侍郎，一个是福建的王庆云，最爱照应同乡，另一个又是他的同年，而且是好友的伺桂清。
en: At that thought, Chunshou shuddered. This was serious! One of Huang's examination classmates, Peng Yunzhang of Suzhou, had already become a grand councillor. There were also the two vice-presidents of the Board of Revenue. One, Wang Qingyun of Fujian, was particularly eager to help men from his home province. The other was He Guiqing, another examination classmate of Huang's and a close friend.

zh: 俗语说得好，“朝里无人莫做官。”黄宗汉敢于如此目中无人，无非仗着内有奥援，而且听说他今年进京，皇上召见六次之多，圣眷正隆，自己无论如何碰不过他。这些念头雷轰电掣般闪过心头，顿感气馁，只得忍气吞声地陪个罪。
en: The saying was true: “Without someone at court, do not seek office.” Huang's arrogance rested on powerful backing in the capital. Moreover, it was said that during his visit there that year the emperor had received him no fewer than six times. He was enjoying exceptional imperial favour. Chunshou could not possibly prevail against him. These thoughts flashed through his mind like thunder and lightning, draining his courage. Swallowing his anger, he could only apologise.

zh: “大人息怒。我岂敢跟大人抬杠？一切还求大人维持。”
en: “Please do not be angry, Your Excellency. How could I dare argue with you? I can only ask for your protection in this matter.”

zh: 这一说，黄宗汉的脸色才和缓了一些，“既为同僚，能维持总要维持。不过，“他使劲摇着头，一字一句地说：”难，难！“
en: Only then did Huang's expression soften a little. “We are colleagues. Naturally, I shall support you wherever I can. But...” He shook his head emphatically and pronounced each word with care. “Difficult. Very difficult.”

zh: 椿寿的心越发往下沉，强自镇静着问道：“大人有何高见？要请教诲。”
en: Chunshou's heart sank further. Forcing himself to remain calm, he asked, “What course would Your Excellency advise? I beg you to instruct me.”

zh: “岂敢，岂敢。等我想一想再说吧！”
en: “Oh, I could hardly presume. Let me think it over first.”

zh: 说完，端一端茶碗，堂下侍候的戈什哈便拉开嗓子：“送客！”
en: With that, Huang lifted his teacup. An attendant waiting below called out loudly, “Show the guest out!”

zh: 这送客等于逐客。椿寿出了抚台衙门，坐在轿子里，只催轿扶加快，急急赶回本衙门，让听差把文案请到“签押房”，关上房门，细说了上院的经过，惊疑不定地问道：“各位看看，黄抚台这是什么意思？”
en: This dismissal amounted to an expulsion. Chunshou left the governor's office and, once in his sedan chair, kept urging the bearers to go faster. Back at his own headquarters, he summoned his secretaries to his private office and shut the door. After describing the interview in detail, he asked in alarm and uncertainty, “What do you think Governor Huang means by all this?”

zh: “黄抚台外号‘黄阎罗’，翻脸不认人是出名的，这件事要好好铺排一下。”
en: “His nickname is Huang the King of Hell. He is notorious for turning on people without warning. This business will need careful handling.”

zh: “唉！”椿寿摇摇头，欲言又止，失悔在黄抚台刚到任，不理他索贿的暗示。
en: “Ah!” Chunshou shook his head, beginning to speak and then stopping. He regretted having ignored Huang's hint about a bribe when the new governor first arrived.

zh: “ ‘天大的公事，地大的银子’，”有个文案说很很率直，“先去探探口气看，院上到底打的什么主意？”
en: “‘A mountain of official business can be moved by a mountain of silver,’” one secretary said bluntly. “We should first sound him out and learn what he really has in mind.”

zh: 于是连夜走路子去打听，总算有了确实的消息，据说黄宗汉为了明年的新漕得以早日受兑装载，照限期抵达通州，决定上奏，把湖属八帮的瘤船追了回来，漕米卸岸入仓，连同明年的新漕，一起装运。
en: They used their connections that very night to make inquiries and eventually obtained definite news. It was said that, to ensure next year's new grain could be accepted and loaded early and reach Tongzhou on time, Huang had decided to petition the throne to recall the boats of Huzhou's eight associations. Their grain would be unloaded and stored, then shipped together with next year's collection.

zh: 这样做法，只苦了漕帮，白白赔上一笔疏浚河道的费用。其次，那些奉委押运的候补州县，没有“公费”可派，一笔过年的盘缠便落空了。椿寿心中虽有不忍，但到底是别人的事，藩司能够不赔，已是上上大吉，只好狠一狠心不理他们了。
en: Such a measure would chiefly hurt the associations, which would have paid for the dredging to no purpose. The expectant magistrates appointed as escorts would suffer too: without official expense allowances to draw upon, the money they had hoped to take home for the New Year would vanish. Chunshou felt sorry for them, but their troubles were, after all, their own. If the provincial treasury could escape a loss, that was already the best he could hope for. He would have to harden his heart and leave them to it.

zh: 果然，第二天抚台衙门来了正式公事，惟恐影响来年新漕的期限，“所有本年湖属八帮漕船，仰该司即便遵照，全数追回，候命办理。”椿寿不敢怠慢，立即派出人去，把湖属八帮的漕船截了回来，同时上院去见抚台，请示所谓“候命办理”是如何办法？
en: Sure enough, an official order arrived from the governor's office the next day. To avoid disrupting the schedule for the following year's grain, “all boats belonging to this year's eight Huzhou associations are to be recalled without delay, in full compliance with this order, and held pending further instructions.” Chunshou dared not hesitate. He immediately sent men to intercept the boats and bring them back, then went to the governor's office to ask what the “further instructions” would be.

zh: 黄宗汉一直托病不见。过了有五、六天，一角公文送到，拆开一看，椿寿几乎昏厥，顿足骂道，“黄寿臣，黄寿臣，你好狠的心！我与你问冤何仇，你要置我于死地！“
en: Huang repeatedly declined to see him, pleading illness. Five or six days later, another official dispatch arrived. Chunshou opened it and almost fainted. Stamping his foot, he cried, “Huang Shouchen! Huang Shouchen! How can you be so cruel? What wrong have I done you that you must drive me to my death?”

zh: 黄宗汉的手段，的确太毒辣了，他以一省最高行政长官的地位，统筹漕运全局的理由，为了使来年新漕的输运，如期完成，以期此后各年均得恢复正常，作了一个决定，本年湖属八帮的漕米，留浙变价，全部漕米二十七万六千石，照户部所定价格，每石二两银子，共该五十五万二千两，限期一个月报缴。
en: Huang's methods were indeed ruthless. Invoking his authority as the province's highest administrative official and his responsibility for the entire grain-transport system, he had issued a decision. To ensure that the following year's grain arrived on schedule and that regular arrangements could thereafter be restored, this year's grain from Huzhou's eight associations would remain in Zhejiang and be sold. The total quantity was 276,000 shi. At the Board of Revenue's prescribed rate of two taels per shi, the proceeds due were 552,000 taels, to be remitted within one month.

zh: 这是椿寿与尖丁早已算过了的，市价与部价的差额，一共要三十三万两银子。如果在他第一次到湖州开会之前，抚台就作了这个决定，那么漕帮赔大部分，藩司赔小部分，这笔小部分的赔款，也还可以在浮收的款项中拨付，说起来只是今年白吃一场辛苦，没有“好处”而已。但现在的情况完全不同了，漕帮负担了疏浚河道的全部经费，事先已经声明，出了这笔钱，漕船非走不可，于今截回不定，已觉愧对漕帮，再要他们分赔差额，就是漕帮肯赔，自己也难启齿，何况看情形是决无此可能的。
en: Chunshou and the headman had already worked out what this meant: the gap between the market price and the official rate was some 330,000 taels. Had the governor made this decision before Chunshou's first meeting in Huzhou, the associations would have borne the larger share and the provincial treasury the smaller. The treasury's portion could still have been drawn from the excess collections. In effect, everyone would merely have worked for nothing that year and forfeited their customary gains. Now the situation was entirely different. The associations had paid the full cost of dredging and had explicitly stipulated that, once the money was spent, the boats must sail. Recalling them already left Chunshou ashamed. He could hardly ask them to contribute towards the price shortfall as well, even if they were willing—which, from all appearances, they certainly were not.

zh: 至于浮收的“好处”，早已按股照派，“分润”有夫人员，哪里再去追索？即使追索得到，也不过五、六万银子，还差着一大截呢！
en: As for the profits from excess collection, those had already been divided into shares and distributed among the people concerned. How could they now be recovered? Even if recovery were possible, they amounted to only fifty or sixty thousand taels, far short of what was needed.

zh: 事情的演变，竟会弄得全部责任，落在自己一个人头上。椿寿悔恨交并，而仍不能不拼命作最后的挣扎，愁眉苦脸地召集了亲信来商议，大家一致的看法是：“解铃还须系铃人”，惟有去求抚台，收回“变价”的成命，应解的二十多万石漕米，随明年新漕一起启运。就这样起卸入仓，从船上搬到岸上，明年再从岸上搬到船上，来回周折的运费、仓费，以及两次搬动的损耗，算起来也要赔好几万两银子，而且一定还会受到处分，但无论如何总比赔三十三万两银子来得好。
en: Events had somehow left the entire burden resting on Chunshou alone. Tormented by regret and anger, he nevertheless had to make one last desperate effort. With a miserable expression, he called his trusted advisers together. They all reached the same conclusion: only the man who had tied the knot could untie it. He must beg the governor to withdraw the order to sell the grain and allow the more than two hundred thousand shi to be shipped with the next year's collection. Unloading it now, storing it on shore, and loading it again the following year would still cost tens of thousands of taels in handling charges, storage fees, and losses from repeated movement. A disciplinary penalty would also be unavoidable. Even so, it would be better than finding 330,000 taels.

zh: 两害相权取其轻，椿寿只得硬着头皮上院，把“手本”送了进去，门上出来答道：“上头人不舒服，请大人回去吧！上头交代，等病好了，再请大人过来相叙。”
en: Choosing the lesser of two evils, Chunshou steeled himself and went to the governor's office. He sent in his visiting card, but the gatekeeper returned with a message. “His Excellency is unwell and asks you to go home. He says he will invite you to call when he has recovered.”

zh: 棒寿愤不可遏，吩咐跟班说：“回去取铺盖！抚台不见我不走，就借官厅的炕床睡。”
en: Chunshou's anger became uncontrollable. “Go back and fetch my bedding,” he told his attendant. “If the governor will not see me, I shall not leave. I can sleep on the couch in the reception hall.”

zh: 门上一看，这不象话，赶紧陪笑道：“大人不必，不必！想来是有急要公事要回，我再到上房去跑一趟。”
en: Seeing how unseemly the situation was becoming, the gatekeeper hastened to placate him. “There is no need, Your Excellency, no need at all! You must have some urgent official matter to report. I shall go to the inner quarters once more.”

zh: 于是椿寿就在官厅中坐等，等了半个时辰，黄宗汉出来了，仰着头，板着脸，一见面不等椿寿开口，就先大声问道：“你非见我不可？”
en: Chunshou waited in the reception hall. After about an hour, Huang appeared, head raised and face stern. Before Chunshou could speak, he demanded loudly, “You insist on seeing me?”

zh: “是！”椿寿低声下气地回答：“大人贵恙在身，本不该打搅，只是实在有万分困难的下情上禀。”
en: “Yes,” Chunshou replied humbly. “I ought not to disturb Your Excellency during your illness, but I am in the greatest difficulty and must explain my circumstances.”

zh: “如果是湖属漕米的事，你不必谈。已经出奏了。”
en: “If it concerns the Huzhou grain, there is no need to say anything. I have already reported the decision to the throne.”

zh: 这句话就如焦雷轰顶，一时天旋地转，不得不颓然坐倒，等定定神看时，黄宗汉已无踪影，抚院的戈什哈低声向他说道：“大人请回吧！轿子已经伺侯半天了。”
en: The words struck him like a thunderbolt. The room seemed to spin, and he collapsed into a seat. When he recovered enough to look around, Huang had vanished. An attendant said softly, “Please go home, Your Excellency. Your chair has been waiting for some time.”

zh: 椿寿闭上眼，眼角流出两滴眼泪，拿马蹄袖拭一拭干净，由听差扶掖着，一步懒似一步地走官厅。
en: Chunshou closed his eyes. Two tears escaped from their corners. He wiped them away with the curved cuffs of his robe and, supported by an attendant, left the hall, each step more reluctant than the last.

zh: 就在这天晚上，椿寿在藩司衙门后院的签押房里，上吊自杀。第二天一早为家人发觉，哭声震动内外，少不得有人献殷勤，把这个不幸的消息，飞报抚台。
en: That night, Chunshou hanged himself in the private office behind the provincial treasury. His household discovered him early the next morning, and their cries of grief filled the compound. Someone inevitably seized the opportunity to curry favour by rushing the unhappy news to the governor.

zh: 黄宗汉一听，知道闯了祸，逼死二品大贝，罪名不轻。但转念想起一重公案，觉得可以如法炮制，心便放了一半。
en: Huang knew at once that he was in trouble. Driving an official of the second rank to his death was no minor offence. Then he remembered an earlier case. If he could follow the same procedure, perhaps he would be safe. The thought eased half his fear.

zh: 他想起的是陕西蒲城王鼎尸谏的往事，这重公案发生在十年以前，王鼎与奸臣穆彰阿，同为大学士值军机。这位“蒲城相国”性情刚烈，嫉恶如仇，而遇到穆彰阿是阴柔奸险的性格，每在御前争执，一个声色俱厉，一个从容自如，宣宗偏听不明，总觉得王鼎不免过分。
en: The case he recalled was that of Wang Ding of Pucheng, Shaanxi, who had taken his own life as a final remonstrance ten years earlier. Wang and the corrupt minister Mujangga had both been grand secretaries serving on the Grand Council. Wang, known as the grand secretary from Pucheng, was fierce in temperament and hated wrongdoing. Mujangga was subtle, yielding in manner, and treacherous. When they argued before the Daoguang emperor, one spoke with visible anger while the other remained composed. The emperor, swayed by one side and failing to see clearly, invariably felt that Wang had gone too far.

zh: 道光二十二年，为了保荐林则徐夏用，王鼎不惜自杀尸谏，遗疏痛劾穆彰阿。那时有个军机章京叫陈孚恩，是穆彰阿的走狗，一看王鼎不曾入值，亦未请假，心里一支，借故出宫，赶到王鼎家一看，听得哭声震天，越发有数。趁王鼎的儿子，翰林院编修王抗骤遭大故，五中昏瞀的当儿，劝他把王鼎的尸首解下来，同时把遗疏抓到手里，一看内容，不出所料，便又劝王抗以个人前程为重，不必得罪穆彰阿，又说“上头”对王鼎印象不佳，而大臣自杀，有伤国体，说不定天颜震怒，不但王鼎身后的恤典落空，而且别有不测之祸。
en: In the twenty-second year of Daoguang, Wang Ding pressed for Lin Zexu's restoration to office and went so far as to hang himself in remonstrance, leaving a memorial that bitterly denounced Mujangga. A Grand Council secretary named Chen Fu'en, one of Mujangga's henchmen, noticed that Wang had neither attended duty nor asked for leave. Growing suspicious, he found an excuse to leave the palace and hurried to Wang's residence. The sound of overwhelming grief confirmed his fears. Wang's son, Wang Kang, a compiler in the Hanlin Academy, was dazed by the sudden calamity. Taking advantage of his confusion, Chen urged him to have the body lowered and at the same time secured the final memorial. Its contents were exactly what he had expected. He then advised Wang Kang to think of his own future and avoid offending Mujangga. He added that the emperor already held a poor opinion of Wang Ding and that a senior minister's suicide damaged the dignity of the state. If the emperor became angry, the family might lose not only the customary posthumous honours but also face unforeseen disaster.

zh: 这一番威胁利诱，教王抗上了当，听从穆彰阿更改遗疏，并以暴疾身故奏报。宣宗也有些疑心，但穆彰阿布置周密，“上头”无法获知真相，也就算了。
en: Threats and promises together deceived Wang Kang. He accepted Mujangga's alteration of the final memorial, and his father's death was reported as the result of sudden illness. The Daoguang emperor had some suspicions, but Mujangga had arranged matters so thoroughly that the truth could not reach the throne. The affair was allowed to rest.

zh: 陈孚恩帮了穆彰阿这个大忙，收获也下小，不久，穆彰阿就保他当山东巡抚。而王抗则以不能成父之志，为他父亲的门生，他自己的同年，以及陕甘同乡所不齿，辞官回里，郁郁以终。
en: Chen Fu'en profited handsomely from this service. Before long, Mujangga recommended him for the governorship of Shandong. Wang Kang, on the other hand, was despised for failing to fulfil his father's purpose—by his father's protégés, by his own examination classmates, and by fellow natives of Shaanxi and Gansu. He resigned, returned home, and died in sorrow.

zh: 穆彰阿是道光十五年乙未科会试的大主考，黄宗汉是他的门生，颇为巴结这位老师。秦桧门下有“十客”，穆彰阿门下有“十子”，黄宗汉与陈孚恩都在“穆门十子”之数，自然熟知其事。所以，一遇椿寿的变故，他立即遣派亲信，以釜底抽薪的宗旨，先设法把椿寿的遗嘱弄到手，然后亲自拜访驻防的将军和浙江学政，因为这两个人是可以专折奏事的，先要把他们稳住，才可以不使真相上闻。
en: Mujangga had been chief examiner at the metropolitan examination in the yiwei year, the fifteenth year of Daoguang. Huang Zonghan was therefore one of his examination protégés and had diligently cultivated his patron. Just as Qin Hui had once had his “Ten Guests,” Mujangga had his “Ten Sons.” Huang and Chen Fu'en both belonged to that circle, so Huang knew the Wang Ding affair very well. As soon as Chunshou's death occurred, he sent trusted men to secure Chunshou's final statement, aiming to remove the danger at its source. He then personally visited the commander of the local banner garrison and Zhejiang's education commissioner. Both were entitled to submit independent memorials to the throne. He first had to secure their cooperation if the truth was to be kept from the emperor.

zh: 当然，另一方面他还要间接拜托旗籍的官员，安抚椿寿的家属，然后奏报藩司出缺。上吊自杀是瞒不住的，所以另外附了个“夹片”，说是“浙江钱漕诸务支出，本年久旱岁歉，征解尤难，该司恐误公事，日夜焦急，以至迫切轻生。”把湖属八帮应运漕米，留浙变价的事，只字不提，同时录呈了经过修改的椿寿的遗嘱。咸丰帝此时初登大宝，相当精明，看遗嘱内有“因情节所逼，势不能生”两句话，大为疑惑，认为即令公事难办，何至遽尔自尽？是否另有别情，命令黄宗汉“再行详细访察，据实奏闻，毋稍隐饰。”
en: Meanwhile, he used intermediaries to ask banner officials to placate Chunshou's family, then reported that the provincial treasurer's post had fallen vacant. The suicide itself could not be concealed. Huang therefore attached a supplementary note: “The administration of Zhejiang's revenues and grain entails many expenditures. This year, prolonged drought and a poor harvest have made collection and remittance especially difficult. Fearing that official business would suffer, the treasurer grew anxious day and night until, overcome by desperation, he took his own life.” He made no mention of the order to retain and sell the Huzhou grain. He also submitted an altered copy of Chunshou's final statement. The Xianfeng emperor, newly enthroned and still quite discerning, was struck by two phrases in it: “Driven by the circumstances, I can no longer live.” Even if official business was difficult, why should it lead so abruptly to suicide? Suspecting another cause, he ordered Huang to “make further detailed inquiries and report the facts, concealing nothing.”

zh: 接着，浙江学政万青藜也有专折奏报，说椿寿身后，留有遗嘱，“实因公事棘手，遽行自尽。”与黄宗汉的奏折，桴鼓相应。皇帝批示：“已有旨，令黄宗汉详查具报。汝近在省垣，若有所闻，亦可据实具奏。”
en: Zhejiang's education commissioner, Wan Qingli, then submitted his own memorial. He stated that Chunshou had left a final declaration and “had indeed taken his own life because official business had become intractable.” This neatly echoed Huang's account. The emperor replied: “An order has already been issued directing Huang Zonghan to investigate thoroughly and report. Since you are in the provincial capital, you too may submit a factual report if anything comes to your attention.”

zh: 看来事情要闹得很大，但事态真正严重的关键所在，只有黄宗汉自己知道。因为椿寿的自尽，如果真的是由于他的措施严峻、则虽良心有愧，亦不过课以道义上的责任，在公事上可以交代得过，那就不必有所畏惧。而事实上并非如此，椿寿之死，是死在他虚言恫吓的一句话上。
en: The affair seemed likely to grow serious, but only Huang knew where the real danger lay. If Chunshou had truly killed himself merely because Huang's administrative measures were severe, Huang might feel guilty and bear moral responsibility, yet he could still defend his official conduct. There would have been little to fear. But that was not what had happened. Chunshou had died because of a false statement Huang had used to intimidate him.

zh: 所谓“留浙变价”，原是黄宗汉有意跟椿寿为难的一种说法，暗地里他并不坚持这样做，不但不坚持，他还留着后手，以防椿寿无法做到时，自己有转圜的余地。
en: The proposal to retain and sell the grain in Zhejiang had been devised to make Chunshou's life difficult. In private, Huang did not insist upon it. Indeed, he had kept another course in reserve so that, if Chunshou could not comply, he himself would still have room to manoeuvre.

zh: 由于在军机处和户部都有极好的关系，所以黄宗汉对来年新漕改用海运，以及本年湖属各帮漕米，不能如限北运的处置办法，都有十足的把握，私底下书函往还，几乎已有成议。但这些情形，椿寿无从知道，他亦瞒着不说。以改用海运并无把握，河运粮船难以依限回空的理由，下令截回漕船，留浙变价，这一套措施与他所奏报的改革办法，完全不符。他向椿寿所说的，留浙变价一事，“已经出奏”，事情到了推车撞壁的地步，再也无可挽回，这才使椿寿感到已入绝路，不能不一死了之。其实，“已经出奏”这句话，根本是瞎说。
en: With excellent connections in both the Grand Council and the Board of Revenue, Huang was entirely confident about securing sea transport for the following year's grain and about the arrangements for this year's Huzhou grain, which could not be sent north within the prescribed time. Private correspondence had already brought these matters close to agreement. Chunshou had no way of knowing this, and Huang deliberately kept him in the dark. Claiming that sea transport remained uncertain and that the canal boats could not return on schedule, Huang ordered the fleet recalled and the grain sold in Zhejiang. These measures were wholly at odds with the reforms he had actually proposed to the throne. When he told Chunshou that the decision to sell the grain had “already been reported,” he made it appear that matters had reached an immovable barrier and that no remedy remained. That was what persuaded Chunshou that he had reached a dead end and could only die. In fact, the claim that the decision had already been reported was a complete fabrication.

zh: 就凭这句谎言，黄宗汉便得对椿寿之死，负起全部责任。因而他必须多方设法掩饰遮盖，不使真相上闻，一面活动万青藜等人，帮着他瞒谎，一面遣派亲信，携带巨贤，到京师活动。当然，象军机大臣彭蕴章那里，是不必也不能行贿的，只有以同年的身份，拜托关顾照应。
en: That lie alone made Huang fully responsible for Chunshou's death. He therefore had to do everything possible to conceal the truth from the throne. While persuading Wan Qingli and others to help sustain the deception, he sent trusted men to the capital with large sums of money to work on his behalf. With someone like Grand Councillor Peng Yunzhang, of course, bribery was neither necessary nor possible. Huang could only appeal to their bond as examination classmates and ask for his protection.

zh: 不过这样一件案子，也不是轻易压得下去的。椿寿是“上三旗”的旗人，亲戚之中，颇有贵官，认为他的死因可疑，自然要出头为他讲话，这样军机处要帮黄宗汉的忙，就不能不费一番手脚，来遮人耳目。
en: Even so, a case like this could not easily be suppressed. Chunshou belonged to the Upper Three Banners and had highly placed relatives. They suspected that his death had a hidden cause and naturally spoke up for him. If the Grand Council was to help Huang, it would have to take some pains to conceal what it was doing.

zh: 照一向的惯例，类似这种情况，一定简派大员密查。既称密查，自然不能让被查的人知道，可是一二品的大员出京，无论如何是件瞒不住的事，于是便有许多掩护其行踪及任务的方法，一种是声东击西，譬如明发上谕：“着派某某人驰往江苏查案”，这人便是“钦差”的身分，所经之处，接待的礼节极其隆重。这样一路南下，到了济南，忽然不定了，用钦差大臣的关防，咨会山东巡抚，开出一张名单，请即传提到案，迅雷不及掩耳地展开了查案的工作。
en: In such circumstances, established practice called for a senior official to conduct a secret investigation. Naturally, the person under investigation was not supposed to know. Yet the departure from the capital of a first- or second-rank official could hardly be hidden. Various methods were therefore used to disguise his route and assignment. One was to announce one destination while aiming at another. A public edict might, for instance, order a named official to proceed urgently to Jiangsu to investigate a case. Travelling as an imperial commissioner, he would receive elaborate honours along the way. On reaching Jinan, however, he would suddenly stop. Using his commissioner's seal, he would send the governor of Shandong a list of people to be summoned immediately, launching the investigation before anyone had time to prepare.

zh: 再有一种是暗渡陈仓，乘某某大员外放到任的机会，密谕赴某处查案。
en: Another method was to use an outwardly ordinary appointment as cover: a senior official leaving the capital to take up a provincial post would receive secret instructions to investigate a case elsewhere on the way.

zh: 这道密谕照例不发“邸抄”，被查的省分，毫无所知，行到目的地，拜访总督或巡抚，出示密谕，于是一夕之间，可以掀起大狱。查黄宗汉逼死椿寿一案，就是用的这一种办法，所以在表面上看不出黄宗汉出了毛病的痕迹。这当然又是军机处帮他的忙。
en: Such instructions were not published in the official court gazette, so the province concerned knew nothing of them. On reaching his destination, the investigator called on the governor-general or governor and produced the secret edict. A major judicial inquiry could thus erupt overnight. This was the method chosen to investigate Huang's role in driving Chunshou to his death. Outwardly, there was therefore no sign that Huang was in trouble—another favour done him by the Grand Council.

zh: 这位钦差名叫何桂清，是黄宗汉的同年。在他们乙未一榜中，何桂清的年纪比较轻，仪表清俊，吐嘱渊雅，人缘极好。这年秋天，由户部侍郎外放江苏学政，在京里饯行送别的应酬甚多，所以一直迟迟不能启程。就在这殷摒挡行囊，准备到任的期间内，出了椿寿这件案子，彭蕴章和他一些在京同年商量的结果，奏请密派问桂清于赴江苏学政途中，顺道查办。“上头”只对椿寿的死因怀疑，不曾想到是他所信任的黄宗汉干的好事，自然不会以何桂清与黄是同年为嫌，便准了军机处的建议。
en: The commissioner chosen was He Guiqing, Huang's examination classmate. Among the successful candidates of their yiwei year, He was relatively young. Handsome, refined in speech, and graceful in manner, he was exceptionally well liked. That autumn he had been transferred from a vice-presidency at the Board of Revenue to the post of education commissioner in Jiangsu. So many farewell engagements awaited him in the capital that his departure was repeatedly delayed. Chunshou's case arose while he was making ready to leave. After consulting other examination classmates in the capital, Peng Yunzhang proposed that He be secretly instructed to investigate it on his way to Jiangsu. The emperor suspected something about Chunshou's death, but had not imagined that Huang, whom he trusted, was responsible. He therefore saw no reason to object to He's relationship with Huang and approved the Grand Council's recommendation.

zh: 这个消息，很快、很秘密地传到了杭州，黄宗汉等于服下一位定心丸。
en: The news reached Hangzhou swiftly and in strict secrecy. To Huang, it was profoundly reassuring.

zh: 何桂清以钦命在身，不敢耽搁，也就在岁暮之际，出京南下。
en: With an imperial commission now entrusted to him, He Guiqing dared delay no longer. As the year drew to its close, he left the capital and headed south.
